title: crossrev finding check
description: What the cross-model check returns: one decision per numbered candidate the prompt carried. The checker runs on the resolver's harness and model, so the model judging a finding is not the model that raised it. The two shapes here are forced by the harnesses rather than chosen: no $schema or $id key, because Claude Code's --json-schema rejects a schema naming the 2020-12 meta-schema and fails before the model is called; and every property listed in 'required', because Codex enforces OpenAI strict mode, which demands it. Genuinely optional fields are therefore nullable rather than absent.

decisions.description: Exactly one decision per candidate the prompt numbered — no more, no fewer, no repeated positions. The orchestrator checks the numbers against the candidates it sent: a candidate left out has no decision recorded, which is a silent loss rather than a visible one.

position.description: The number shown beside the candidate in the prompt — 1 for the first, 2 for the second, and so on. A small integer rather than the finding's 16-character id, because copying a hash accurately is clerical work models are poor at and a mistyped one is accepted silently.

decision.description: confirmed: the finding holds against the code and posts. rejected: the finding is wrong and stays off the pull request. duplicate: the finding is the same point as another candidate, named in duplicate_of, and folds into it.

duplicate_of.description: The position this candidate duplicates, or null unless decision is duplicate. The chain must end at a confirmed candidate: a duplicate of a duplicate is fine, a duplicate of a rejected candidate and a cycle are not.

reason.description: One line saying why: the evidence the decision rests on, in at most 300 characters. A duplicate names what makes the two the same point; a base-versus-head explanation comes before any pre_existing correction.

severity.description: The severity the candidate should have carried, or null when the reviewer's stands. A correction, not a second opinion filed beside the first: it replaces the severity before the finding posts.

pre_existing.description: Whether the defect would still exist if this pull request were reverted, or null when the reviewer's stands. A correction with the same force as severity: it replaces the value before the finding posts, and the reason explains the base-versus-head reading behind it.
